minutes.headline: Committee approved the high school program of studies and line item transfers; FY24 budget got only an update.
minutes.summary: The committee heard public comment on the social emotional learning program, approved line item transfers and the high school program of studies for 2023-24, and received the superintendent's report. The FY24 budget update was brief, with no recommended changes yet pending the town's insurance rate and state aid. The committee also reviewed its goals and discussed the Turkey Hill and primary school facilities questions.

public_comment.topic: Introduced himself as the new finance committee liaison taking over from Evan.
Asked what changed between November and December on opting out of the SEL program, and whether parents can opt out of SEL woven into regular classroom curriculum.

votes.motion: Approve minutes of November 2 as presented (November 16 deferred for lack of quorum)
Approve line item transfers as presented
Accept the LHS program of studies modifications

budget_items.what_was_said: Business manager presented transfers on three sheets: paraprofessional money shifted among schools as students moved, a chemical hygiene officer stipend funded from a middle school nurse surplus, and other reconciliations.

High school guidance software funds shifted to middle school contracted services for i-Ready; athletic insurance increased; unemployment claims were unusually high; natural gas and computer services accounts topped up from facilities accounts.
A member noted the overlay account accumulates, with last year's addition and the current balance stated, and said it is likely small relative to lakefront abatement needs.
figures_as_heard: a hundred and sixteen thousand dollars
a little over two hundred and eighty thousand dollars

budget_items.what_was_said: Business manager said the town manager discussion touched on ESSER-funded positions expiring at the end of next year and a strategy for which to maintain.
Chapter 70 is still being calculated pending the Governor's budget; administration's recommended changes hinge on the health insurance rate expected mid-February to early March.
A member said capital funds don't sunset, but if the project isn't feasible the money should be returned as unexpended capital given the town's finances.

transfers.description: Reconciling sub accounts: substitutes accounts, elementary paraprofessionals to primary, middle and high school; middle school nurse surplus to school stipends for chemical hygiene officer
High school guidance software to middle school contracted services; athletic insurance, unemployment, dues, natural gas and computer services accounts adjusted from other accounts

Superintendent to ask the consultant for the equity audit final report for the February 1 meeting, with discussion of recommendations on February 15.

what_happened.line: The committee approved the high school program of studies modifications for 2023-24 by a 3-0 roll call vote.
The committee approved a set of local-budget line item transfers as presented, also 3-0 by roll call.
The FY24 budget update made no recommended changes, pending the health insurance rate and the state's Chapter 70 aid calculation.
The business manager said ESSER-funded positions expire at the end of next year, and a strategy for which to maintain was discussed with the town manager.
The November 16 minutes were carried over because a quorum of those present at that meeting was lacking.

why_it_matters: The FY24 school budget is not yet set: two outside inputs, the health insurance rate and state aid, decide how large the gap is that the town's tax bill has to cover.
Positions now paid from temporary ESSER federal funds expire after next year, which is a mechanism by which their cost can move onto the town budget, mostly taxes, unless they are cut or kept.
watch_next: The health insurance rate, expected mid-February to early March, which the administration's recommended budget changes depend on.
The February 1 meeting, where the equity audit final report and the acronym list are due, with recommendations discussed on February 15.
